scenario_description:
Objective: Complete the cold, ground-level stovepipe cleanout before Owen leaves with the holiday transport.
Emerging Need: The cleanout has started, but the unpacked borrowed brush is rectangular and cannot fit the round pipe; nothing has broken or become lodged.
Decision Context: Retrieve the6-inch poly brush and matched-rod specification, then arrange the confirmed free-loan kit while Owen can collect it. Do not improvise with metal tools, buy equipment or light the stove unfinished.
Consequence: After the loan desk closes and Owen leaves, the intended supported cleanout cannot finish today; the safe fallback is to keep the stove cold.

parameter.title: Wood stove stovepipe cleanout
parameter.description: Brush the interior stovepipe tee and reset the cap before the evening cold snap.

parameter.content: The stove is cold, the tarp is down, and the interior tee cap is off. We are unpacking the borrowed cleanout kit before inserting anything into the pipe.

We stopped the cleanout: the borrowed box contains a flat rectangular fireplace brush, not a round stovepipe brush. Nothing has been inserted or broken. Owen can collect a compatible loan kit on his town errand, but will leave for family lunch at 14:15.

parameter.subject: Holiday tool cabinet: matched stovepipe kits available
parameter.body: The local no-charge tool cabinet has matched round poly-brush/rod kits in several diameters. Email the exact kit code and diameter for a free hold, naming Owen Vale for collection if desired. Holds and pickup finish at 13:00 today; unclaimed kits then go to the closed holiday storeroom. No purchase or chimney service is included.

parameter.content: The tool desk closed at 13:00 without a kit set aside for us. I have left for family lunch and will not be back until tomorrow. The mismatched brush is packed away, the stove remains cold, and today's cleanout is unfinished.
